newsitem.title: USA: SmithKline says Kytril available in new form.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline says Kytril available in new form.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc said Tuesday its antiemetic Kytril is now available in a new four milliliter multidose vial.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted marketing clearance for the new multidose vial on May 31.
Kytril, which is also available in a tablet form and a single-dose vial, is for the prevention of nausea and vomiting associated with certain emetogenic cancer therapies.
The company said fear of nausea and vomiting are major concerns of patients receiving chemotherapy for cancer.

The company said the Kytril four mL multidose vial makes weight-based dosing more efficient and minimizes wasted product. In addition, it helps to conserve resources, contain costs and make better use of storage space.
The company said the most frequently reported adverse effects of Kytril in controlled trials were headache, asthenia, somnolence, diarrhea, constipation and fever.
